title_zh: ShadowFormer：全局上下文有助于图像阴影去除
problem_statement: Existing deep shadow removal methods often suffer from severe artifacts around shadow boundaries and inconsistent illumination because they focus locally and ignore the global contextual correlation between shadow and non-shadow regions.

contributions.text: We introduce a Retinex-based shadow model that formulates the degradation and motivates exploiting global contexts for shadow removal.
We propose ShadowFormer, a lightweight single-stage transformer network built on a multi-scale channel attention framework for end-to-end shadow removal.

We design a Shadow-Interaction Module (SIM) with Shadow-Interaction Attention (SIA) in the bottleneck stage to exploit global contextual correlations between shadow and non-shadow regions across spatial and channel dimensions.
We achieve state-of-the-art performance on ISTD, ISTD+, and SRD datasets using up to 150x fewer model parameters compared to existing methods.

method_overview: ShadowFormer is a transformer-based network derived from a Retinex-based shadow model, designed to restore shadow-free images by leveraging global context. It employs a multi-scale encoder-decoder architecture using Channel Attention (CA) modules to efficiently capture hierarchical information. At the bottleneck stage, a Shadow-Interaction Module (SIM) utilizes Shadow-Interaction Attention (SIA) to model the correlation between shadow and non-shadow regions, allowing uncorrupted non-shadow areas to guide the restoration of shadowed areas for better illumination consistency and boundary artifact reduction.

experiments.main_results: ShadowFormer achieves state-of-the-art performance on all three datasets while using 5x to 150x fewer model parameters than competing methods.
takeaways: The proposed method effectively addresses boundary artifacts and illumination inconsistency by leveraging global context from non-shadow regions
proving that transformer-based architectures with specific interaction modules are highly efficient for partial corruption tasks like shadow removal.

full_analysis_md: # ShadowFormer: Global Context Helps Image Shadow Removal ## 1. Problem Statement Image shadow removal is challenging due to arbitrary shadow patterns and spatially non-uniform degradation, which leads to illumination and color inconsistencies. Existing deep learning methods often focus locally, resulting in boundary artifacts and ignoring the global contextual correlation between shadow and non-shadow regions. ## 2. Methodology The authors propose **ShadowFormer**, a lightweight transformer-based network derived from a **Retinex-based shadow model**. This model posits that shadow and non-shadow regions share the same reflectance but differ in illumination, motivating the use of non-shadow regions to guide shadow restoration. ### Key Components: - **Multi-scale Encoder-Decoder**: Built with **Channel Attention (CA)** modules to efficiently capture global information and hierarchical features. - **Shadow-Interaction Module (SIM)**: Located at the bottleneck stage, it introduces **Shadow-Interaction Attention (SIA)**. This mechanism exploits global contextual correlations across spatial and channel dimensions, using the uncorrupted non-shadow regions to inform the restoration of shadowed areas. ## 3. Experiments and Results Extensive experiments were conducted on three public datasets: **ISTD**, **ISTD+**, and **SRD**. - **Performance**: ShadowFormer achieves state-of-the-art results in terms of PSNR and SSIM. - **Efficiency**: The model is significantly lighter, requiring **5x to 150x fewer parameters** than existing SOTA methods. - **Visual Quality**: The method effectively reduces boundary trace artifacts and ensures better illumination consistency compared to prior works. ## 4. Conclusion ShadowFormer demonstrates that leveraging global context through a specialized transformer architecture can solve the partial corruption problem in shadow removal more effectively and efficiently than previous multi-stage or heavy models. The Retinex-based theoretical foundation provides a strong motivation for the proposed Shadow-Interaction Module. ## 5. Code The code is available at: [https://github.com/GuoLanqing/ShadowFormer](https://github.com/GuoLanqing/ShadowFormer)
